record_identity.title: French supermarket refrigeration controllers compromised and perishable stock destroyed

incident_identity.historical_event_name: French supermarket refrigeration controllers compromised and perishable stock destroyed
incident_identity.date_basis: Reporting dates initial disruption to the night of 11–12 October; the 13 October authority update describes continuing compromise risk. No definitive campaign end date is established.

summary: French supermarket refrigeration systems were compromised during the night of 11–12 October 2026. Retailers reported altered cooling or defrost operation and discarded food. CERT-FR confirmed numerous controller compromises and expanded its warning to several product families on 13 October. Reuters reported at least 350 affected stores. Later reporting described intervention and further stock loss at Dixell-equipped stores; a specialist inferred automation from rapid setting changes. One Intermarché director recounted the destruction of approximately US$112,000 in food and the ensuing cleanup. Authorities and manufacturers issued containment and restoration guidance. The attacker and exact initial-access method remain unestablished. A contemporaneous Dutch online-services disruption is not treated as the same occurrence.

vigil_assessment.factual_basis: The national response alert establishes actual controller compromises. Retailer accounts and independent reporting establish physical food loss and disrupted retail operations at bounded stores, beyond an unexploited vulnerability. The record groups the reported French refrigeration attack wave while preserving distinct product families and store outcomes. Claroty's earlier vulnerability research is background, not forensic attribution for the October attacks. Le Monde quotes a specialist who inferred automation because settings changed several times per second. This does not establish AI assistance, fuzzing or the initial-access method.
vigil_assessment.governance_interpretation: Unauthorised changes to refrigeration control translated a digital access failure into spoiled physical goods and interrupted food retail. The reported operational consequences span multiple businesses. AI participation remains unknown. The case is admitted as a maintainer-requested cyber-physical context occurrence, not as proof of AI misconduct. AI-assisted automated fuzzing is an unverified hypothesis; an automated attack could also use conventional scripts or known vulnerabilities.
vigil_assessment.significance_to_cam: A connected control surface can convert unauthorised configuration changes into material physical consequences. This provides a bounded comparator for AI-enabled security and infrastructure governance while keeping the actual attack method, affected controller generations and AI attribution open.
assessment_boundaries: AI assistance, autonomous agents and automated fuzzing have not been established by occurrence-specific evidence.
A specialist inferred automation from rapid setting changes. Automated parameter alteration is not itself evidence of AI-assisted fuzz testing.
No attacker attribution or common exploit chain across every affected store is proven.
The August AK-SM 800A research is not proof of the exploit used in the October attack wave or against older controller families.
The separate Dutch retailer online-services incident is excluded; initial European headlines do not establish a common campaign.
Reported store counts use different dates and definitions and are not a count of people harmed.
The approximately US$112,000 loss is a published affected-party account, not an independently audited or cross-store extrapolated figure.
No confirmed illness, death, starvation or lasting population-wide food deprivation is established.

Admission is explicitly authorised by the maintainer despite the unresolved AI nexus; it does not adopt the separate pending constitutional proposal or broaden other incident admissions automatically.

source_records.evidence_status_basis: Reporting includes named refrigeration specialists and contrasting store outcomes.
